def: Turning an image of text into the characters it shows, together with their positions and a confidence for each.
The characters, fonts and positions stored in a born-digital PDF, which can be read exactly without any OCR.
Converting a grey or colour scan to pure black and white by choosing a threshold that separates ink from paper.
Finding where the text is on a page and returning boxes or polygons for lines or words, before any character is read.
The number of single-character substitutions, deletions and insertions needed to turn the OCR output into the reference, divided by the reference length.
The same edit-distance measure as character error rate, computed over words instead of characters.
A convolutional recurrent neural network that reads a whole text line as a sequence of image slices without segmenting individual characters.
A loss and decoding rule that adds a blank class so a network can label each image slice and be trained on text alone, without alignments.
The extra class meaning no new character here, which separates repeated letters and is deleted when decoding.
An engine's own estimate of how likely a character, word or line is to be right, used to route uncertain results to review.
An error whose output is well-formed and plausible, such as a vision-language model changing one digit of an amount, so it passes format checks and proofreading for sense.
The share of extracted fields whose value equals the reference exactly, used where a single wrong character changes the meaning.
